# Yuanbao xCard Express Prompt

## Compact Express Quick Reference

Use this short section before the long component catalog. It is the mental model for one-shot Yuanbao freeform xCards.

Final answer shape when prose is useful: plain text, then a raw A2UI block, then more plain text. Do not add Markdown/code fences around the A2UI block.

Here is your card:
<a2ui>
$/title = "任务清单"
$/items = [{label: "整理记录", value: "已完成"}, {label: "复核时间表", value: "待处理"}]
item = Column(children=[
  Text($label),
  Text($value, variant="caption")
])
root = Card(Column(children=[
  Text($/title, variant="h4"),
  List(_template($/items, item))
]))
</a2ui>
You can adjust the items as needed.

- The `<a2ui>` block must be raw inline text, not a Markdown/code fenced block.
- Inside `<a2ui>` write A2UI Express only: data assignments, component variables, and exactly one `root = ...` component.
- Do not write JSON UI schemas such as `{"type":"list"}` or `{"type":"product_card"}`; those are not Express and fail because they do not define `root`.
- For repeated data, do not index with `$/items[0]`; define an item template and render it with `List(_template($/items, item))`. Inside the template use relative bindings such as `$label` and `$value`.
- `Text.variant` is only `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `h5`, `caption`, `footnote`, or `body`. Do not use `body1`, `body2`, `title`, `subtitle`, or `headline`.
- Prefer the simple component set unless the user asks for a richer interaction: `Card`, `Column`, `Row`, `Text`, `Image`, `Button`, `List`, `_template`, and `Event`.

# A2UI Express DSL Output Contract

You must output the user interface using A2UI Express.

IMPORTANT: In a Yuanbao final answer, embed exactly one raw `<a2ui>...</a2ui>` block directly in the text. Plain prose may appear before or after the block when useful, but the block itself MUST NOT be wrapped in Markdown/code fences. When passing Express to a tool `express` parameter, pass only the raw body without `<a2ui>` tags.

The host compiler will compile your A2UI Express output into the correct JSON envelopes automatically.

## Grammar Rules

1. Component constructors can be assigned to variables or nested inline inside parent component arguments:
   header = ComponentA(prop1="val1")
   root = ComponentB([header, ComponentC("Click", action=Event("submit"))])

   Keyword arguments (`param=value`) and positional arguments with `_` placeholders are supported.

   Variable names MUST start with a letter or underscore, and only contain letters, digits, and underscores.

2. The interface tree must have a single entry point assigned to the reserved variable 'root'.

3. Primitives:
   - Strings: Quoted with `"` or `"""`. Support for `\n`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"` escapes.
     Raw Strings: Prefaced by `r` (e.g., `r"..."` or `r"""..."""`), with no escape processing.
   - Numbers: write as integers or decimals, e.g., 42
   - Booleans: write true or false
   - Null values: write null
   - Dates & Times: Values for date-time inputs (e.g. in DateTimeInput) must strictly use RFC 3339 format with a timezone offset (e.g. "2026-03-14T00:00:00Z").

4. Lists: represent as arrays, e.g., [child1, child2].

5. Maps: represent as key-value blocks, e.g., {title: "Overview", child: contentCol}. Map keys are always literal strings (dynamic variable resolution is not supported for keys).

6. Data bindings: prefix absolute paths in the data model with '$', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   Prefix relative list scopes with '$', e.g., $firstName.
   A lone '$' represents an empty relative path which resolves to the root of the current context (e.g. inside a template, representing the entire item itself).

7. Logic and validation: prefix client check rules with '?', e.g., ?required or ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$"). To specify a custom error message for validation failures, append it as an extra string argument, e.g. ?regex("^[0-9]{5}$", "Postal code must be 5 digits").

8. Action events: represent server-side actions using the Event helper:
   Event("save_deal", {rep: $/form/rep})

9. Nested functions: call client functions directly using catalog signatures, for example myFunction("value").

10. Data model population: Assign a value directly to an absolute data path (e.g. $/path/to/key = "value") to populate or initialize values inside the shared dataModel. The value can be a primitive, array, or map.

11. Dynamic list templates: If a component expects a template child list, represent it using the _template helper:
    _template($/path/to/list, itemTemplate)
    And define the template component variable on another line, utilizing relative path references prefixed with $:
    itemTemplate = Image($url)

13. Static properties: Arguments annotated with '(static)' in the signatures below MUST be defined as literal values or arrays inline. You CANNOT use a dynamic data binding path (prefixed by $) for these arguments.

14. Required actions: Parameters named 'action' (or annotated in component signatures) are strictly required. You must pass a valid Event (e.g. Event("click")) or function call. If no specific action is described in the user request, you must provide a dummy click event like Event("click") instead of passing null or omitting the parameter.

15. Surface targeting: Output `surface(surfaceId)` to specify or target a user interface surface:
    surface("dashboard-surface-1")
    root = Button(...)

## Positional Component Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate components. Do not output property keys:
• Box(contentAlignment? (static), children, style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - contentAlignment: Where children sit inside the box. Defaults to `topStart`. Must be one of: 'topStart', 'topCenter', 'topEnd', 'centerStart', 'center', 'centerEnd', 'bottomStart', 'bottomCenter', 'bottomEnd'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick
• Button(child (static), action? (static), enabled?, variant? (static), checks? (static), style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - action: An interaction handler: either an agent-side event or a renderer / agent function call, never both.
  - enabled: Whether the button answers taps. `false` draws the disabled state (the whole button at 40% opacity unless style.disabled says otherwise, same size), ignores every gesture including combinedActions, skips checks and hides their message, swallows the touch, and reports the button as disabled to accessibility. A Button inside a disabled component is disabled too, whatever this says. A value that is missing, fails to resolve or is not a boolean counts as true.
  - variant: Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick

• ChoiceGroup(options (static), value, variant? (static), indicator? (static), toggleArea? (static), focusInputOnSelect? (static), optionEnabled?, action? (static), indicatorAlign? (static), selectedEffect? (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - Description: Selects one or more options, each drawn by a template component fed with the option's uiData. The group owns the selection state, the item frame and the selection indicator; the template only draws content.
  - options: Option data together with the option template.
    Map keys:
    * items - Path to the option array in the data model; literals and function calls are not accepted. Each entry is { uiData, value }: uiData is a plain object (not a binding) that relative paths in the template resolve against; value is a string unique within the group.
    * componentId - Component id of the option template, instantiated once per option and scoped to its uiData.
  - value: Values of the selected options. Always a string array; at most one entry in mutuallyExclusive.
    Map keys:
    * @path - JSON Pointer into the data model.
  - variant: Must be one of: 'mutuallyExclusive', 'multipleSelection'
  - indicator: How selection is shown. `control` draws a radio or check control and only that control toggles selection (see toggleArea); `border` wraps each option in a container, outlines the selected ones, and the whole option toggles selection; `none` draws no frame or control, the whole option toggles selection, and the template shows the selected state itself through `@selected`. Must be one of: 'control', 'border', 'none'
  - toggleArea: What a tap toggles on when indicator is `control`: only the control, or the whole option. Ignored for `border` and `none`, where the whole option always toggles. Components inside the template that declare their own action still answer the tap themselves. Must be one of: 'control', 'option'
  - focusInputOnSelect: When a user taps an option to select it, focus the first TextField in that option and open the keyboard. Does not focus on initial render or when selection changes through data binding. Tapping inside a TextField retains its normal focus behavior; deselecting an option never requests focus.
  - optionEnabled: Whether one option answers the user, evaluated in each option's scope: relative paths read that option's uiData, `@index` is its index and `@selected` its current state. `false` makes the option ignore taps on its frame, control and template, keeps its selection exactly as it is, disables every component in its template the way `enabled` does, reports it as disabled to accessibility, and draws the group's `style.disabled.effect` over the whole option (frame, outline and control included), 40% opacity by default. A disabled group disables every option whatever this says. A value that is missing, fails to resolve or is not a boolean counts as true.
  - action: Runs after each user tap on an option, once the selection has been written back to `value`, including a tap on an already selected option in mutuallyExclusive. It runs in the tapped option's scope: relative paths read that option's uiData, `@index` is the option index and `@selected` its new state. Changes to `value` that do not come from a tap do not run it. The renderer starts it with invokeAction("option:<i>"), where i is the option's position among the rendered options.
  - indicatorAlign: Side the control sits on. Only used when indicator is `control`. Must be one of: 'start', 'end'
  - selectedEffect: Visual effect over the whole rendering of a selected option: template content, control, and in border mode the frame fill and outline. Visual only; the option stays interactive. `dimmed` overlays the basic_container_primary color at 70% opacity. Must be one of: 'dimmed'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column.
• Clickable(child (static), action? (static), enabled?, checks? (static), style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))

  - enabled: Whether the tap area answers taps. `false` draws its content at 40% opacity unless style.disabled says otherwise, ignores every gesture including combinedActions, skips checks, swallows the touch, and reports it as disabled to accessibility. It cascades: every component inside is disabled as well. A value that is missing, fails to resolve or is not a boolean counts as true.

A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.

• ConditionView(value (static), cases (static), default? (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - value: Value compared against each case match.
  - cases: List of maps with keys:
    * match - Literal string, number, or boolean. Same type within one component.

• DotIndicator(count, current?, interactive? (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - Description: A row of dots with one highlighted, for a Pager or any other paged content. Linked to nothing but the data model: bind current to the same path as the Pager's currentPage, and count to the array the pages come from. Decorative unless interactive.
  - count: How many dots. A number is floored; bound to an array it is the array's length. Held to 0–50.
  - current: Index of the highlighted dot, from 0. Out of range is shown clamped and not written back. Defaults to 0.
  - interactive: When true, tapping dot i writes i to current, which turns a Pager bound to the same path. Defaults to false.
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
• FlowColumn(children, justify? (static), align? (static), style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - Description: Lays children out top to bottom and moves to the next column when the current one is full. Requires style.height. Without style.width it is as wide as its columns, up to the space it is given.

  - align: Cross-axis alignment of items inside their own line. A line is as thick as its thickest item. Must be one of: 'start', 'center', 'end'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

• HorizontalGrid(children, rows? (static), style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - Description: A lazy grid with a fixed number of rows, like Compose LazyHorizontalGrid with GridCells.Fixed(n): only the columns in or near its viewport are rendered, and columns scrolled away are disposed, so keep any state that must survive scrolling in the data model. `rows` decides the rows; columns are added toward the end side. Needs a bounded height, usually style.height. Children are stretched to the height of their cell and keep their content width. As wide as its columns up to the width it is offered, or up to 2048dp inside a horizontal List; beyond that it scrolls sideways inside itself.

• Label(text, variant? (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - Description: A short single-line tag: the text on a rounded fill tinted from the text color at 8%. Size, padding and corner come from `variant`; the copy truncates with an ellipsis rather than wrapping. Not tappable: wrap it in Clickable for that. Use Text for copy without a fill.
  - text: The tag's copy, as plain text on one line. Markdown is not interpreted. An empty string draws nothing.
  - variant: Size step: `large` is 11/15 type on 3×6 padding with a 6 corner, `small` is 10/13 type on 2×4 padding with a 4 corner. Defaults to small. Must be one of: 'large', 'small'
  - style: How the component is drawn. `padding` is space outside the fill. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

• Pager(children, currentPage?, loop? (static), autoPlay? (static), userScrollEnabled? (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - Description: Horizontal pages that snap one at a time, like Compose HorizontalPager. Each child is a page as wide as the pager (less 2 × (peek + pageSpacing) when peek is set); only the pages in or next to the viewport are rendered, and pages swiped away are disposed, so keep any state that must survive in the data model. At most 50 pages. Takes the width it is offered; as tall as style.height / aspectRatio, otherwise as its tallest rendered page. Has no indicator of its own: bind currentPage and a DotIndicator to the same path. Gestures belong to a Clickable inside a page, not to the pager.
  - currentPage: Index of the page shown, from 0. Bound to a path it is two-way: a swipe, an autoPlay step or a DotIndicator tap writes the new page there, and writing the path from outside (updateData, updateDataModel) animates the pager to it. Floored, then wrapped when loop is on and clamped to the last page when it is not; the corrected value is written back. Defaults to 0.
  - loop: Joins the last page to the first, so swiping and autoPlay never stop. No effect with fewer than 2 pages. Defaults to false. Literal only.
  - autoPlay: Advances one page every interval once the pager has settled. Without loop, the last page goes back to the first. Pauses while touched, while the pager is off screen or the app is in the background, and never runs when the system asks for reduced motion. Unset does not auto-play.
    Map keys:
    * interval - Milliseconds between pages. Below 2000 is raised to 2000.
  - userScrollEnabled: Whether a swipe turns the page. False still lets currentPage and autoPlay turn it. Defaults to true.
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
• PlatformSwitch(condition (static), weight? (static))
  - Description: Picks one child tree by host formFactor. Each condition value is a component id defined in the same list (e.g. mobile-root). Missing the current key falls back to mobile.
  - condition: Keys are formFactor tokens. Values are component ids, not layout names. desktop and web may point at the same id.
    Map keys:
    * mobile - Fallback tree when the current formFactor key is missing.
    * ios - iPhone tree. Host formFactor=ios.
    * android - Android phone tree. Host formFactor=android.
    * harmony - HarmonyOS phone tree. Host formFactor=harmony.
    * tablet - Component id of the tablet tree.
    * desktop - Component id of the native desktop tree, e.g. wide-root.
    * web - Component id of the web tree. May reuse the same id as desktop.
    * tv - Component id of the TV tree.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
• RichText(spans (static), variant? (static), style?, maxLines? (static), weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - Description: One paragraph made of styled spans. Spans flow, wrap and truncate together as one block. A span may carry its own action; a span with an action and no style.color is drawn in basic_text_link. Markdown is not interpreted. Use Text when the copy has a single style.
  - spans: The runs of the paragraph, in reading order. A literal array: each span's text and style may be bound, the array itself may not.
  - variant: Size, line height and default style of every span. Unset inherits the container's text style, falling back to body. Must be one of: 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'caption', 'footnote', 'body'
  - style: How the component is drawn, and the default text style of every span. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - maxLines: Maximum number of rendered lines. Zero means no limit. Spans cut off by the ellipsis are not tappable.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick
• Row(justify? (static), align? (static), children, style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - justify: Must be one of: 'start', 'center', 'end', 'spaceBetween', 'spaceAround', 'spaceEvenly'
  - align: Must be one of: 'start', 'center', 'end', 'stretch'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick
• Stepper(label?, value, min?, max?, step?, style?, weight? (static))
  - label: Label shown before the numeric controls.
  - value: Bound numeric value updated by the controls.
  - min: Minimum allowed value. Defaults to 0.
  - max: Maximum allowed value. Defaults to 100.
  - step: Amount added or subtracted per tap. Defaults to 1.
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
• SvgView(url?, urlDark?, source?, sourceDark?, description?, fit? (static), style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - Description: Draws one SVG document, either inline (source) or from an https URL (url). Exactly one of those two is set. Android decodes it with Coil 3 coil-svg, iOS with SDWebImageSVGCoder, and Web with the browser's SVG-as-image decoder. The guaranteed markup is the static visual subset of SVG 1.1. The box comes from style and the parent; a missing axis follows the decoder's intrinsic aspect ratio. fit places the decoded image in that box and defaults to contain. style.tint, when set, tints the decoded image with that token.
  - url: https URL of an SVG document. Mutually exclusive with source. Same shapes as Image url.
  - urlDark: Optional dark-mode document for url. Used when the host is in dark mode; missing or empty falls back to url. Ignored unless url is set.
  - source: Inline SVG document. Mutually exclusive with url. Passed to the platform decoder as bytes. UTF-8 size after resolution is at most 65536 bytes.
  - sourceDark: Optional dark-mode document for source. Same fallback rule as urlDark. Ignored unless source is set. UTF-8 size after resolution is at most 65536 bytes.
  - description: Accessibility name for the graphic. Empty and without an action, the view is decorative.
  - fit: How the decoded image is placed inside the content box. Does not change the box size. Defaults to contain. Must be one of: 'contain', 'cover', 'fill', 'none'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick
• Switcher(value, content (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - value: The selected item. `content` and everything that renders the selection binds under this path.
    Map keys:
    * @path - JSON Pointer into the data model
  - content: What the selected item is shown in. Each distinct value keeps its own scroll position.
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
• Text(text, variant? (static), style?, maxLines? (static), weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - text: The text to display, as plain text. Markdown is not interpreted: `**bold**` renders with its asterisks. Use `variant`, `style.fontWeight` and `style.textDecoration` for emphasis, and separate components for structure.
  - variant: Must be one of: 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'caption', 'footnote', 'body'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - maxLines: Maximum number of rendered lines. Zero means no limit.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick
• TextField(value?, placeholder?, variant? (static), appearance? (static), checks? (static), style?, weight? (static))
  - value: The value of the text field. Bind a path for the typing to be written back.
  - placeholder: The placeholder text for the input field.
  - variant: The type of input field to display. Must be one of: 'longText', 'number', 'shortText', 'obscured'
  - appearance: How the field is drawn. `filled` is the design system's capsule (or block for longText): a fill, an outline, a trailing clear / reveal button. `underline` draws no fill, outline, corner or trailing button: the text sits in body type on a hairline, as tall as one line plus 4dp, so it reads as part of the sentence it is placed in — the `Other: ____` of a ChoiceGroup option. Single-line variants only; `longText` keeps the filled block. Typing into a TextField inside a ChoiceGroup option selects that option, whatever its appearance. Must be one of: 'filled', 'underline'
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
• VerticalGrid(children, columns? (static), style?, weight? (static), combinedActions? (static))
  - Description: A lazy grid with a fixed number of columns, like Compose LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Fixed(n): only the rows in or near its viewport are rendered, and rows scrolled away are disposed, so keep any state that must survive scrolling in the data model. `columns` decides the columns; rows are added downward. Takes the full width it is offered. Children are stretched to the width of their cell and keep their content height. As tall as its rows up to its style.height, or up to 2048dp when nothing bounds it; beyond that it scrolls vertically inside itself.
  - columns: The number of columns, as with `GridCells.Fixed(n)`. The columns share the width equally. Defaults to 2. Literal only.
  - style: How the component is drawn. Anything left out stays at whatever the design system already decided.
  - weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
  - combinedActions: Per-gesture actions. Mutually exclusive with action. At least one gesture, and every one of them is a full Action — the same shape the action property takes. A gesture left out is not an action: invoking it fails rather than falling back to click, so a Column that binds only longPress stays untappable. The nearest component that declares any gesture answers the touch and it stops there, so a tappable child inside a tappable container runs the child's action alone. A gesture name this renderer does not know is ignored rather than rejected, which is what lets a card bind one a later renderer will add.
    Map keys:
    * click
    * longPress
    * doubleClick

## Positional Function Signatures

Use these exact positional signatures to instantiate check rules or logic functions:
• add()
  - Description: a + b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• closeModal()
  - Description: Close the Modal with this literal id. Nested modals inside it close with it.
• contains()
  - Description: True when the array values holds an element deeply equal to value. Numbers compare by value. A values that is not an array yields false.
• copyContent()
  - Description: Copy content onto the host clipboard.
• equalsNumber()
  - Description: True when a == b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• equalsString()
  - Description: True when string a equals string b. Null operands coerce to empty string.
• filter()
  - Description: The elements of items whose field equals any element of in, in their original order. A missing field reads as null. A non-array items yields []; a non-array in is treated as a one-element array.
• greaterThan()
  - Description: True when a > b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• greaterThanOrEqual()
  - Description: True when a >= b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• isEmpty()
  - Description: True when value is null, empty string, empty array, or empty object.
• join()
  - Description: Joins the display text of each element of values with separator. With field, each element contributes the first listed field that is not empty. Null, empty strings, objects and arrays are skipped without leaving an extra separator.
• lessThan()
  - Description: True when a < b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• lessThanOrEqual()
  - Description: True when a <= b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• map()
  - Description: Map a data-model array in order. items must be a path binding. Evaluate template once per item in that item's scope; relative paths, @index and @indexValue refer to the item, absolute paths retain the model root. Empty arrays return []; non-arrays and failed item evaluations fail the whole call. Object and array literals in template are evaluated field by field, so a template can build one object per item. Does not write to the data model.
• multiply()
  - Description: a * b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• openHostRoute()
  - Description: Open an in-app route. Engine forwards args.route to the host; BizModel routes it. The triggering component's metadata.extensions is delivered separately to the host dispatcher, not inside args.
• openUrl()
  - Description: Open an http(s) URL. Engine forwards args.url to the host; BizModel opens it. The triggering component's metadata.extensions is delivered separately to the host dispatcher, not inside args.
• openWechatMiniProgram()
  - Description: Open a WeChat mini program from the host App via OpenSDK (WXLaunchMiniProgramReq). Not wx.navigateToMiniProgram (that JSAPI is mini-program to mini-program and uses appId).
• publishDataModel()
  - Description: Hand this surface's whole data model to the host as an action named publishDataModel, with the snapshot in context.dataModel. The host uploads it; the renderer sends nothing itself.
• rendererVersionAtLeast()
  - Description: True when the host rendererVersion is a semver at least version.
• repeatQuery()
  - Description: Repeat the current Yuanbao chat request. The optional params object is merged into the repeated request. For an action FunctionCall, the triggering component's metadata.extensions is delivered separately to the host dispatcher, not inside args.
• select()
  - Description: Evaluates and returns then when condition is true, else otherwise (null when else is omitted). Only the chosen branch is evaluated. The result may be any JSON value, including a whole style object.
• sendQuery()
  - Description: Host follow-up prompt. Engine forwards action.functionCall args to the host; BizModel sends the prompt. The triggering component's metadata.extensions is delivered separately to the host dispatcher, not inside args.
• sequence()
  - Description: Run actions in order. Each action is parsed just before it runs.
• setTimeout()
  - Description: Run action after delay milliseconds. Cancelled when the surface is destroyed.
• subtract()
  - Description: a - b. Null operands coerce to 0.
• switch()
  - Description: Run the first case whose literal match equals value, or default.
• toast()
  - Description: Show a host toast with message.
• updateData()
  - Description: Atomically write entries into this surface's data model. Null value deletes the path.
• urlEncode()
  - Description: Percent-encode value per RFC 3986 unreserved set. Spaces become %20.
• yb_chat_repeat()
  - Description: Wire name `repeatQuery` was published under before the camelCase names existed. Same behaviour, and it reaches the host under this name rather than as `repeatQuery`, which is what lets a card written for an older Yuanbao keep working on it. Write `repeatQuery` in new documents.
• yb_chat_send_prompt()
  - Description: Wire name `sendQuery` was published under before the camelCase names existed. Same behaviour, and it reaches the host under this name rather than as `sendQuery`, which is what lets a card written for an older Yuanbao keep working on it. Write `sendQuery` in new documents.
• yb_navigation_open_host_route()
  - Description: Wire name `openHostRoute` was published under before the camelCase names existed. Same behaviour, and it reaches the host under this name rather than as `openHostRoute`, which is what lets a card written for an older Yuanbao keep working on it. Write `openHostRoute` in new documents.
• yb_navigation_open_url()
  - Description: Wire name `openUrl` was published under before the camelCase names existed. Same behaviour, and it reaches the host under this name rather than as `openUrl`, which is what lets a card written for an older Yuanbao keep working on it. Write `openUrl` in new documents.

## Catalog Instructions

Use this Yuanbao xCard catalog for compact interactive cards.

Generate self-contained cards only. Do not use WebCard, xCardTemplate, tracking, host environment values, or undeclared host functions.

Prefer restrained Yuanbao visual hierarchy: clear text, token colors, modest spacing, no unsupported gradients, shadows, blur, transforms, or raw colors.

Expose a single root component named root. Put visible completion feedback in the card and include a human-readable resultText in every event context.

## Yuanbao OpenClaw Runtime Contract

- Default path: for a one-shot freeform card, directly embed exactly one raw `<a2ui>...</a2ui>` block containing Express in the final answer. Plain prose may appear before or after it when useful, but never wrap the block in Markdown/code fences. The plugin intercepts it and sends one xCard; the user never sees the DSL. This path cannot self-correct, so keep the Express simple and valid.
- The block content is A2UI Express, not JSON. Do not output invented schemas such as `{"type":"list"}` or `{"type":"product_card"}`; use data assignments plus `root = Card(...)`.
- Tool path: call `yuanbao_xcard_send` / `yuanbao_xcard_update` with the `express` parameter when you need waitForAction, explicit mode/audience/title, an update to an existing surface, or same-turn retry after compiler errors. Pass only the raw Express body: no `<a2ui>` tags, Markdown fences, JSONL envelopes, or prose.
- Generated cards must be self-contained. Do not depend on WebCard, xCardTemplate, tracking, host environment values, or undeclared host functions.
- Include a visible post-action result state. Every `Event(...)` context must include stable business values and a human-readable `resultText`.
- For follow-up changes to an existing generated card, prefer updating the original surface when the runtime provides a surface id; do not create a replacement card for the same business state.
